text.p: The privatisation offer of Poland's Bank Handlowy was heavily oversubsubscribed in both retail and institutional tranches with foreign demand exceeding $3.5 billion, the issue's lead manager said on Wednesday.
Krzysztof Opawski, head of Schroders Polska, told a news conference the offering was three times oversubscribed in the retail offer and 17.4-times oversubscribed in the institutional offer.
He said the public offering would bring into the treasury's coffers about 1.3 billion zlotys ($402 million).
Opawski said that Handlowy's public offer had lured scores of international financial institutions including some newcomers to Poland.

"(International institutions) placed more than 600 bids worth more than $3.5 billion and among those interested there were investment funds and pension funds and for some institutions it was their first investment in Poland," he said.

The biggest demand, 31 percent of the total, came from the British market, with U.S. investors accounting for 26 percent of demand. Bids from Polish institutional investors made up about 2 percent of the total demand, he added.
